item.text:
**2B.10 Research Note: Net Regional/International Peace, Stability, and Lawfulness**

Bottom line: **mixed, slightly positive only if inherited conflicts and constraints are fully credited**. Biden in 2024 pushed ceasefires, crisis de-escalation, alliance consultation, and nonproliferation discipline, which points toward greater stability and lawfulness in several theaters. But the inherited Gaza and Ukraine wars persisted, and U.S. support to Ukraine included bounded escalation. I found **no clean evidence of a broadly more peaceful world order by year-end**, only a better-managed but still dangerous set of conflicts.

| Polarity | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Positive | Secretary Blinken’s Meeting with Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu | U.S. Department of State | 2024-05-01 | https://2021-2025.state.gov/secretary-blinkens-meeting-with-israeli-prime-minister-netanyahu-4/ | The administration publicly pushed an immediate Gaza ceasefire tied to a hostage deal, stressed humanitarian aid, urged Israel not to widen the conflict, and said it wanted a lasting, sustainable peace. This is direct evidence of trying to leave a key inherited conflict more lawful and stable. | 2B.10, 2B.7, 2B.4, 2B.5, 2B.1 |

Even if unsuccessful, this is evidence of pursuing a lawful settlement rather than normalization of open-ended war. | 2B.10, 2B.7, 2B.1 |
| Positive | Joint Press Statement on the Signing of the Nuclear Consultative Group Guidelines | U.S. Department of Defense | 2024-07-11 | https://www.defense.gov/News/Releases/Release/Article/3835633/joint-press-statement-on-the-signing-of-the-nuclear-consultative-group-guidelin/ | The U.S. and ROK formalized principles and procedures for nuclear deterrence and operations, strengthening structured consultation and reducing alliance drift or unilateral escalation on the Korean Peninsula. That supports a more stable and rule-bound regional order. | 2B.10, 2B.7, 2B.5, 2B.6 |

That is evidence of institutionalized crisis management rather than improvisation, which tends to stabilize great-power and alliance relations. | 2B.10, 2B.7, 2B.5, 2B.6 |
| Positive | US urged countries to pass messages to Iran against escalation, State Dept says | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-07-28 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/us-urged-countries-to-pass-messages-to-iran-against-escalation-state-dept-says-3555469 | The administration used diplomatic channels to warn Iran not to escalate and to support ceasefire and hostage-release efforts. That is direct evidence of trying to prevent a wider regional war. | 2B.10, 2B.7, 2B.1, 2B.6 |
| Negative | The US quietly shipped long-range ATACMS missiles to Ukraine | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-04-24 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/the-us-quietly-shipped-longrange-atacms-missiles-to-ukraine-3394976 | Secretly sending longer-range missiles expanded Ukraine’s strike options and increased the conflict’s escalation envelope. This is counterevidence to a simple “more peaceful than inherited” reading, even if framed as deterrence. | 2B.10, 2B.2, 2B.7, 2B.8, 2B.9 |

It was defensive in framing, but it still widened the war’s operational scope. | 2B.10, 2B.2, 2B.7, 2B.8, 2B.9 |
| Negative | 56th Security Consultative Meeting Joint Communique | U.S. Department of Defense | 2024-10-30 | https://www.defense.gov/News/Releases/Release/Article/3951794/56th-security-consultative-meeting-joint-communique/ | The communique portrayed DPRK, Russian-DPRK arms trade, and alliance deterrence as serious threats and emphasized an expanded U.S. military posture, including nuclear capabilities, to defend the ROK. This is stabilizing in one sense, but it also shows the year did not end with simple demilitarization or pacification. | 2B.10, 2B.5, 2B.7, 2B.8 |

**Assessment**
- Strongest pro-2B.10 evidence: Gaza ceasefire diplomacy, Iran de-escalation, and formal U.S.-ROK consultation mechanisms.
- Strongest anti-2B.10 evidence: Ukraine escalation measures, which widened the conflict envelope even if they were bounded and defensive.
- I found **no evidence that 2024 produced a cleanly more peaceful international environment overall**. The best-supported reading is that Biden **managed inherited conflicts more lawfully and stably than a laissez-faire approach would have**, but did **not** resolve them or clearly leave the system broadly more peaceful by year-end.

**Search gap**
- I did not find a single credible source showing a net, cross-theater improvement in international peace comparable to an actual postwar settlement.
- The main missing piece is hard evidence that the inherited Gaza, Ukraine, and Iran/Korea security situations were all left materially calmer by the end of 2024; the record instead shows partial stabilization plus continued high-risk conflict.
